sumInsured: As per Policy Schedule (not specified in provided extract)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: The eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'No limit', which means that there is no separate restriction on Room Charges incurred towards stay during Hospitalization
great.explanation: Room rent is on a 'No limit' basis, so there is no separate cap on the room category/charges during hospitalization. This helps you avoid room-rent based reductions and lets you choose the room you need.

great.name: ICU Charges
great.quote: Intensive Care Unit Charges (ICU Charges): The eligible ICU Charges applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'No limit', which means that there is no separate restriction on ICU Charges incurred towards stay in ICU during Hospitalization.
great.explanation: ICU charges are covered on a 'No limit' basis with no separate cap for ICU stay during hospitalization. This reduces the risk of large ICU bills becoming out-of-pocket (subject to Sum Insured).

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses.
great.explanation: Base Sum Insured can be reinstated unlimited times in a policy year, and the recharge can be used for the same illness as well as different illnesses. This is very strong for multiple hospitalizations in the same year.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: enhance the Sum Insured by 50% flat... (vi) In the event of a Claim there is no impact on the accrual of Cumulative Bonus.
great.explanation: Sum Insured increases by a flat 50% as Cumulative Bonus, and a claim does not impact the accrual of this bonus. This helps your cover grow without getting reset due to claims.

good.name: Built-in SI Buffer
good.quote: The Recharge shall be utilized only after the base Sum Insured, applicable Cumulative Bonus , Cumulative Bonus Super (if applicable) and Plus Benefit (if applicable) have been completely exhausted in that Policy Year.
good.explanation: Recharge becomes available only after the base Sum Insured and applicable bonuses/benefits are fully exhausted in that policy year. This works as an extra buffer for large or multiple claims, but it is not usable from the first rupee.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/ treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Listed named ailments/surgeries are not covered until you complete 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a standard market waiting period for specific conditions.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded until 36 months (3 years) of continuous coverage from the first policy inception with the insurer. This is within the common 2–4 year range, so plan for this waiting period if you have known conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days from policy commencement, while accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard initial waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: For a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for 60 days immediately before the date of hospital admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: For a period of 180 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for 180 days immediately after discharge from the hospital. This supports follow-up care and medicines for up to 6 months after hospitalization.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person... for the Medical Expenses incurred towards Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization (treatment at home that would otherwise require hospitalization) is covered as per policy conditions. This can be useful when hospital admission is not possible or not advisable.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person up to the amount as specified in Policy Schedule , for the Reasonable and Customary Charges necessarily incurred on availing Air Ambulance services
good.explanation: Air ambulance charges are covered up to the amount specified in the Policy Schedule. This can help in emergencies, but the payable limit depends on the schedule.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure  I to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.reference: Clause 4.2(1) + Annexure I (List of Expenses Generally Excluded)
bad.explanation: Items listed as non-medical/consumables in Annexure I are excluded from cover. This can increase out-of-pocket costs for common hospital items during a claim.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: For diseases or conditions or procedure that have a specified sub-limit then all related expenses shall be covered up to the sub-limit specified for that disease or condition or procedure.
bad.explanation: Where the Policy Schedule specifies a disease/condition/procedure sub-limit, all related expenses are payable only up to that sub-limit. This can significantly reduce claim payouts for those listed treatments.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: The Co-payment proportion ( If opted ) shall be borne by the Insured Person on each Claim
bad.reference: General Conditions Applicable To All The Benefits And Optional Benefits, point 4 + Optional Benefit 3.2.7
bad.explanation: If the co-payment option is opted, you must bear the co-payment proportion on each claim. This directly increases your share of every hospitalization bill, so it is a negative feature even when optional.
